G1168.d: from δειλία; to be timid:--be afraid.

G1077.d: neuter plural of a derivative of γένεσις; birthday ceremonies:--birthday.

G1130.d: from a derivative of γυμνός; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad:--be naked.

G1128.d: from γυμνός; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively):--exercise.

G1019.d: from βραδύς; to delay:--be slack, tarry.

G1294.d: from διά and στρέφω; to distort, i.e. (figuratively) misinterpret, or (morally) corrupt:--perverse(-rt), turn away.

G1143.d: a prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively) thwart:--bite.

G1411.d: from δύναμαι; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself):--ability, abundance, meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work.

G1429.d: from δώδεκα and φυλή; the commonwealth of Israel:--twelve tribes.

G1271.d: from διά and νοῦς; deep thought, properly, the faculty (mind or its disposition), by implication, its exercise:-- imagination, mind, understanding.

G1080.d: from a variation of γένος; to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate:--bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring.

G1131.d: of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative):--naked.

G1368.d: from διά and (to filter); to strain out:--strain at (probably by misprint).

G1401.d: from δέω; a slave (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary; frequently, therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency):--bond(-man), servant.

G1272.d: from διά and ἀνοίγω; to open thoroughly, literally (as a first-born) or figuratively (to expound):--open.

G1033.d: from the base of βιβρώσκω; food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law:--meat, victuals.

G1404.d: probably from an alternate form of (to look); a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate):--dragon.

G1389.d: from δόλος; to ensnare, i.e. (figuratively) adulterate:--handle deceitfully.

G1476.d: from a derivative of (to sit); sedentary, i.e. (by implication) immovable:--settled, stedfast.

G1032.d: a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush:--send forth.

G1483.d: adverb from ἐθνικός; as a Gentile:--after the manner of Gentiles.

G1218.d: from δέω; the public (as bound together socially):--people.

G1008.d: from βόσκω; herbage (as if for grazing):--herb.

G1477.d: from a derivative of ἑδραῖος; a support, i.e. (figuratively) basis:--ground.

G1107.d: from a derivative of γινώσκω; to make known; subjectively, to know:--certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.

G1295.d: from διά and σώζω; to save thoroughly, i.e. (by implication or analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.:--bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save.

G1206.d: from δεύτερος; secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day:--next day.

G1229.d: from διά and the base of ἄγγελος; to herald thoroughly:--declare, preach, signify.

G1060.d: from γάμος; to wed (of either sex):--marry (a wife).
